proposed_english: depart upward / be raised up / ascend
rationale: Recurring verb (lines 2, 5, 14, 20-21) consistently paired with ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward' in contexts of apostolic ascent out of the world. Likely Lycopolitan form related to ϫⲓⲥⲉ 'raise/be high' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲭⲥⲉ 'the Height'). 'Depart upward' preserves both motion and direction.
ⲙⲛⲧ- abstract + ⲛⲁⲃ (Lyc. = ⲛⲏⲃ 'lord/master'). The apostle's institutional dominion over his church during his earthly tenure.
Contracted Lycopolitan form of ϫⲟⲉⲓⲥ 'lord/master'. Distinct from but parallel to ⲛⲁⲃ. In line 6 'without master, without shepherd' it pairs with ϣⲱⲥ in the institutional-leadership doublet.

Compound ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who') + ⲭⲁ- ('set/place') + ⲙⲁⲓⲧ ('way/path' = Sah. ⲙⲟⲉⲓⲧ). Literally 'one who sets the way' — a trail-blazer or guide. Used of post-apostolic successors who lead the community after the apostle's departure.
Coptic ϩⲟⲩⲣⲓⲧ 'guard, watchman'. Functions in line 11 alongside ⲃⲟⲏⲑⲟⲥ 'helpers' as institutional roles preserving the church.

proposed_english: his vessels of import / imported wares
rationale: ⲡⲉϥ-ϩⲛⲁⲩ 'his vessels/containers' + ⲛ̄-ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'of bringing/import.' Used in the merchant typology for the apostle returning home with multiplied wares.
ⲙⲛⲧ- abstract + ⲉϣⲱⲧ 'merchant.' The state/profession of being a merchant. Used in apostolic-merchant typology line 19-20.
Variant of ⲧϩⲉ 'manner, fashion.' Used as discourse marker introducing parallel/typological comparisons: 'the manner in which X' (lines 17, 20, 28, 32). Distinct from ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲛ 'Deep' or ⲛⲁⲟ 'great.'
From ⲡⲓⲥⲉ 'to cook, to ripen.' Agricultural-typological term for fruits coming to maturity. Lines 27, 30 (verb), 26 (noun).
Possibly plural of ⲉⲃⲣⲁ 'seed' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲃⲣⲉ 'seed') — the fruits/seed-products that the farmer reaps in Pharmouthi. Line 32.
